query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue Q2 fiscal 2027 year-over-year growth drivers
normalized: 2027 center data drivers fiscal growth nvidia over q2 revenue year

output.content:
NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue was **$89.0 billion in Q2 FY2027** (quarter ended July 26, 2026), a **117% year-over-year increase** from **$41.1 billion in Q2 FY2026**—an incremental **$47.9 billion** of revenue. [[1]] [[2]]

**Primary drivers of the year-over-year growth**

- **Broad-based AI-infrastructure buildout:** NVIDIA attributed demand to a global expansion of AI compute infrastructure across hyperscalers, AI labs, AI-native companies, enterprises, and sovereign customers; management characterized the outlook as supply-constrained. [[3]]

- **Continued Blackwell demand at hyperscalers:** The hyperscale subsegment generated **$49 billion** in Q2 FY2027 and grew **13% sequentially**, driven by sustained strength in Blackwell products. [[3]]

- **Exceptional expansion of ACIE customers:** ACIE—AI clouds/neoclouds, industrial, and enterprise customers—delivered **$40 billion**, up **138% year over year** and **25% sequentially**. [[3]] The principal catalysts were neocloud capacity additions serving enterprises, AI startups, and sovereign customers, plus hyperscalers purchasing external capacity to supplement their internal deployments. [[3]]

- **Faster, lower-cost AI-factory deployment:** NVIDIA said neocloud partners using its DSX reference designs were bringing capacity online faster and at lower token cost, supporting ACIE adoption and revenue growth. [[3]]

- **Sovereign-AI investment:** Sovereign-AI business, mainly through regional neoclouds, rose **more than threefold year over year** in Q2, adding a meaningful demand vector outside the traditional large-cloud cohort. [[3]]

- **Networking and CPU attach:** Networking revenue reached a record and rose **18% sequentially**, while Spectrum-X Ethernet grew **2.6x year over year**; separately, rising agentic-AI adoption accelerated data-center CPU demand, with Grace CPU trailing-12-month revenue exceeding **$5 billion**. [[3]] 

In short, the 117% growth was not solely a GPU-cycle effect: it combined Blackwell-led hyperscale spending with a rapidly scaling, more diversified ACIE ecosystem—especially neocloud, enterprise, startup, and sovereign-AI deployments—along with higher networking and CPU content per AI data-center build. [[3]]
